ads.copy: If you owe more than $10,000 in credit card debt, the government has a program that could cut it in half. Takes 2 minutes to see if you qualify.

Warning: If you're paying multiple credit cards, you may qualify for a program that combines them into one $0 interest payment.
The credit card companies are legally required to do this if you ask — but they'll never bring it up themselves.
She was $83,000 in debt after a divorce. Two years later: zero balances, 690 credit score. Her strategy ↓
Are you drowning in credit card interest? See if you qualify to reduce your debt by up to 50% — takes 90 seconds.

We negotiated $34,000 down to $11,200 for this client. He paid it off in 18 months. Free eligibility check below.
I'm a bankruptcy attorney and I'm telling you — most people filing for bankruptcy don't need to. There's a better option.
Laid off. Maxed out. I made one phone call and my debt was resolved. Real story, real numbers inside.
3 signs your credit card debt is about to become unmanageable — and what to do before it does.
Not bankruptcy. Not a loan. A program that legally reduces what you owe. See if you qualify in 2 minutes.

dna.oneLineSummary: Insider secret frame ('don't want you to know') + specific settlement ratio creates conspiratorial trust and urgency

dna.targetPersona: People overwhelmed by a specific large debt number who want a realistic path

dna.targetPersona: People with damaged credit who feel shame and believe they can't recover

winnerSummary: Debt relief ads with the longest run durations share three patterns: (1) **Specific numbers everywhere** — exact debt amounts ($47k, $83k), settlement ratios (25 cents on the dollar, 50% reduction), and timelines (27 months, 90 seconds to qualify). Vague promises don't run long; specificity does. (2) **Fear + relief in one breath** — the best-performing hooks agitate the fear (drowning in interest, stuck on minimums) then immediately imply effortless escape (one phone call, 2-minute check). The tension-release cycle drives clicks. (3) **Legal and authority framing** dominates over personal testimonials — 'government program', 'legally required', 'bankruptcy attorney says' all outperform pure UGC in this vertical because trust is the primary objection. The winning angle gap is **proactive pre-crisis targeting** (the 'warning signs' format) rather than waiting for the audience to be in full panic mode.
